facts.fact: Original order remains six signed long byte counters: protocol upload,payload upload,protocol download,payload download,DHT upload,DHT download. Only the actual original interfaces and complete Base are compiled; global/DHT/Core/session owner construction is source-only.

Each Date query enumerates UTC daily pathnames selected by its start/end day; within each opened file, record eligibility uses the entire requested interval, not an extra clipping to the pathname day. Nonnull accepter disables month/day cache paths; the end>=now clamp still applies. All new fixture dates are before fixed2030.

Writer rollover appends the pending non-start line to the prior file before switching. Thus a whole multi-day Date-range query can include a next-day reconstructed spill from that prior file, whereas seven independent clipped one-day queries can omit it. P04-19 intentionally exposes only the latter and produces no aggregate/week total. Both month and year rollover fixtures characterize exclusion per member day, not a whole-week query.

Positive s anchors only; s0/negative deactivates. Valid inactive records are ignored. Each anchored delta/e advances exactly one reconstructed minute; e timestamp/version do not replace that clock and e does not clear the source anchor. Baselines are parsed but not usage; overlapping reconstructed minutes add and signed adjustments remain signed.

Original UI TS_WEEK is7*24*60*60seconds and uses TS_HOUR buckets:168 hours, current-time/hour-rounded range plus span offsets, payload-only chart with pixel-dependent merging/scaling. This is not seven selected UTC day rows and has an original whole-span total. None of those graph/total paths is implemented or runtime-qualified by P04-19.

Original PT_SLIDING_WEEK uses now minus multiplier*week; PT_CURRENT_WEEK uses default-timezone GregorianCalendar and configurable long.term.stats.weekstart. This overload config hook is fail-closed in the oracle and is never called. Explicit UTC end-minus6 calendar dates are a deliberate different bounded presentation.

Java permissively skips records/errors and has unchecked multiplication/sums, ignores versions and inactive record field validation. Native retained exact-shape/VERSION1/all-record/checked-arithmetic/bounds/cancellation policies deliberately differ. Presence/observations/strict errors get zero Java equality credit.
